issues.reason: "The surface tense decides, mechanically" - the clause copula is present, and "retired" already has its own licensed participle-as-adjective atom (Member bridges retired), so the Past wrapper both breaks the tense rule and withdraws the present membership the sentence actually asserts (a retired major general still is one).

The half that stands is that nothing records that he is no longer a shuttle pilot (privative "former" has no carrier - the reviewer's own gap); the half that falls is calling the wrapper unlicensed, since "a former shuttle pilot" entails he WAS one, so (Past (Member bridges shuttle_pilot)) is true and well-typed and the calibration line protects it as improvisation in gap territory.

Gap territory by the reviewer's own gap 2 (the compound and naming rules conflict for a proper-noun modifier), and the breton_tapestry precedent fuses a capitalized origin modifier into the compound with no separate named entity, so no atom here is false or ill-typed.

gaps_confirmed: privative / non-subsective adjectives ("a former shuttle pilot") - no encoding for "was but is no longer a P"; the participle-as-modifier route only yields positive properties

a proper-noun modifier inside a common-noun compound ("Air Force major general") - the capitalized run is only part of the phrase, and the compound rules and the mandatory-Name rule pull opposite ways
new_gaps: coordinated predicate NPs under one copula where only the second carries a privative ("is a retired X and a former Y") - the single surface tense cannot be split per conjunct, so a per-conjunct temporal wrapper has no stated licence
repair_summary: Removed the (Past ...) wrapper from bridges_maj_gen, leaving (Member bridges air_force_major_general) at the clause's present tense beside the already-emitted (Member bridges retired); statement 4's Past wrapper on the "former shuttle pilot" conjunct was left as is, since it is the only true trace of the privative and no atom in it is false.
notes: The two Past wrappers get opposite verdicts on purpose: "retired" has a licensed property atom that the wrapper duplicates and distorts, while "former" has none, so there the wrapper is the parse's only (true, if incomplete) record.
